strengths: Applies the recent MeanFlow formulation to text-to-audio generation (TTA), avoiding the need for multi-step teacher distillation or running multiple models during distillation training.

The proposed instantaneous-to-mean training curriculum (pre-training with conditional flow matching and fine-tuning with flow field mix-up) effectively addresses the training instability and slow convergence associated with mean flow optimization.

Impressive efficiency and performance trade-offs: achieves state-of-the-art single-step audio synthesis results on AudioCaps with only 120M backbone parameters and an RTF of 0.013 on consumer-grade hardware (NVIDIA RTX 3090).
Thorough ablation studies analyzing the curriculum stages, flow field mix-up ratios, and integrated classifier-free guidance scales.
weaknesses: Evaluation is limited to a single dataset (AudioCaps test set). Evaluating on additional standard benchmarks such as Clotho would provide a much more convincing demonstration of generalizability.

Lack of subjective human evaluation (e.g., MOS or preference tests for perceptual quality and text-audio alignment). Standard automated metrics (FAD, KL, CLAP) have known biases, particularly when CLAP embeddings are also utilized as conditioning signals.

The core mathematical framework of MeanFlow and integrated CFG is largely adopted from Geng et al. (2025); the primary conceptual contribution lies in its domain adaptation to TTA and the two-stage curriculum strategy.

Minor inconsistencies and missing details in the manuscript: the RTF is reported as 0.013 in Figure 1/Table 1 but stated as 0.016 in the introduction text; Table 2 references 'all four datasets' whereas only three datasets (AudioCaps, Clotho, WavCaps) are described in the datasets section.

strengths: First application and adaptation of the Mean Flow formulation to text-to-audio generation, circumventing the need for expensive multi-step teacher distillation pipelines.

The proposed instantaneous-to-mean curriculum with flow field mix-up provides an effective and well-motivated solution to the training instability and slow convergence often seen with Mean Flow objectives.

Strong empirical efficiency and performance: with only 120M parameters, the model achieves impressive single-step generation metrics and an RTF of 0.013 on a single consumer GPU, while retaining competitive multi-step performance.
Clear writing, well-structured presentation, and thorough ablation studies validating the necessity of the curriculum, flow mix-up ratio, and CFG formulation.
weaknesses: Lack of subjective human evaluation (e.g., MOS or MUSHRA tests for audio fidelity and text-audio alignment), which is standard and critical in audio generative modeling given the known limitations and biases of objective metrics like FAD and CLAP score.
Evaluation is restricted to the AudioCaps test set; benchmarking on additional datasets (such as Clotho) or testing out-of-domain generalization would make the empirical findings more comprehensive.

Methodological novelty is somewhat incremental, as the underlying formulation of Mean Flows, integrated classifier-free guidance, and r=t boundary degradation are adopted directly from Geng et al. (2025), with the main contributions centering on architectural tailoring and curriculum staging for audio.

strengths: The adaptation of the Mean Flow formulation to text-to-audio (TTA) generation is mathematically sound, well-motivated, and avoids the computationally expensive teacher-student distillation pipelines common in few-step generation.

The proposed instantaneous-to-mean training curriculum and flow field mix-up directly resolve training instabilities and slow convergence when learning average velocity fields on audio latents, supported by thorough ablations in Tables 2 and 3.

The model achieves compelling inference efficiency: with only 120M parameters, it reaches a real-time factor (RTF) of 0.013 on an RTX 3090 while outperforming existing single-step and few-step accelerated baselines across standard objective metrics (FAD, FD, KL, CLAP).
Training classifier-free guidance (CFG) directly into the velocity target allows guided sampling without requiring double the function evaluations (NFEs) during inference.
weaknesses: The evaluation relies exclusively on objective automated metrics (FAD, FD, KL, IS, CLAP); incorporating subjective human listening tests (e.g., MOS for audio quality and text-audio alignment) is standard in generative audio and would substantially strengthen the empirical claims.

Experimental evaluation is limited to the AudioCaps test set; evaluating zero-shot generalization on additional benchmarks such as Clotho or MusicCaps would better demonstrate the robustness of the learned flow trajectory across diverse sound domains.

Minor presentation inconsistencies, such as typos in the Table 1 caption ('mulit-step') and a discrepancy in Table 2 referencing 'all four datasets' when three primary datasets are detailed in the Datasets section.

strengths: Addresses a crucial bottleneck in text-to-audio generation (inference latency) by demonstrating high-fidelity single-step (1-NFE) generation without relying on expensive teacher-student distillation.

The proposed instantaneous-to-mean curriculum combined with flow-field mix-up provides an effective solution to the training instability and poor convergence typically encountered when training Mean Flows from scratch.

Integrating classifier-free guidance directly into the average velocity training target eliminates the need for an additional unconditional forward pass at test time, preserving a true 1-NFE inference with a remarkably low real-time factor (RTF 0.013).

Extensive experimental results and ablations across multiple metrics (FD, FAD, KL, IS, CLAP) and tasks (audio and music generation) clearly substantiate the design choices, including the mix-up ratio, curriculum, dual text encoders, and ConvMLP blocks.
weaknesses: Core theoretical foundations of Mean Flows and integrated guidance derive directly from prior work (notably Geng et al., 2025), making the contribution primarily an effective domain adaptation and architectural combination for audio latent modeling.

The subjective human evaluation sample size is relatively limited (10 audio professionals evaluating only 10 prompts/samples per model), which introduces potential variance into the human assessment results.

The paper lacks an explicit discussion or empirical measurement of the training memory and runtime overhead incurred by computing the Jacobian-Vector Product (JVP) during training relative to standard conditional flow matching.

strengths: MeanAudio achieves impressive inference speed (RTF of 0.013 on an RTX 3090) and sets a new state-of-the-art benchmark for single-step text-to-audio generation, substantially outperforming prior accelerated methods like ConsistencyTTA and AudioLCM.

The proposed instantaneous-to-mean training curriculum and flow-field mixup strategy are well-motivated and empirically proven to resolve severe training instabilities encountered when training mean flow models directly on audio latent representations.

Integrating classifier-free guidance (CFG) directly into the average velocity training objective enables true 1-step (1-NFE) generation without requiring paired conditional/unconditional passes at test time.

The experimental validation is thorough, including comprehensive ablation studies on the flow mixup ratio, model architecture components (CLAP vs. T5, ConvMLP, RoPE), CFG scales, as well as scalability experiments on model size and dataset size.
weaknesses: Conceptual algorithmic novelty is somewhat incremental, as the work primarily adapts the recently proposed Mean Flows framework (Geng et al., 2025) and Flux-style MMDiT architectures from vision/multimodal domains into the audio domain.

The scale of human evaluation is somewhat limited; specifically, the subjective evaluation in Table 2 involves only 10 listeners rating 10 samples each, and the dual-encoder human study in Appendix C.1 relies on only 10 captions with 3 listeners, which lacks statistical power and confidence intervals.

The model is restricted to fixed 10-second audio crops; while RoPE theoretically supports variable lengths, empirical validation and generation quality on arbitrary/longer durations are not demonstrated.

strengths: Substantial inference acceleration and efficiency: MeanAudio achieves state-of-the-art single-step generation performance (1-NFE) with a real-time factor (RTF) of 0.013 on an RTX 3090, markedly outperforming previous accelerated TTA baselines (such as ConsistencyTTA and AudioLCM) in both objective metrics and subjective evaluations.

Compact and accessible architecture: At only 120M parameters, the model is significantly smaller than contemporary diffusion/flow baselines (typically 500M to 1.2B parameters) and is trainable on consumer-grade hardware (4x RTX 3090 GPUs in ~3 days).

Well-motivated training innovations: The paper thoughtfully adapts the Mean Flow formulation to audio generation, incorporating an instantaneous-to-mean curriculum with flow-field mixup that prevents training instability, as well as an integrated classifier-free guidance (CFG) mechanism that preserves 1-NFE sampling without extra compute.

Comprehensive experimental analysis: The empirical evaluation covers a broad spectrum of objective metrics (FD, FAD, KL, IS, CLAP), human evaluations, scaling experiments (both data and model size), text-to-music generalization (MusicCaps), and thorough ablations for each architectural and training choice.
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: The core methodology largely builds on the recent Mean Flow framework (Geng et al., 2025) and Flux-style MMDiT architectures (Esser et al., 2024; Hung et al., 2024), adapting these principles to the latent audio domain rather than introducing fundamentally new generative mathematical formulations.

Small-scale human subjective evaluation: The listening tests rely on 10 participants rating 10 samples each (and only 3 listeners for the long-caption evaluation in Appendix C.1). While audio experts were recruited, expanding the sample pool and prompt coverage would lend greater statistical significance to the human evaluation claims.

Fixed-length representation and metric discrepancies: The current implementation is constrained to fixed 10-second segments, and certain metric behaviors are left unanalyzed (e.g., in Table 7, scaling data in MeanAudio-S-Full worsens FAD from 1.77 to 2.85 at 1-NFE despite improvements in FD, KL, and CLAP).
